title: A morphism of short exact sequences lifts to a morphism between any two horseshoe resolutions
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. For a short exact sequence $S:0\to A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ of $\mathcal A$, call a *horseshoe resolution* of $S$ a datum $(s_A,s_B,s_C,\alpha,\beta)$ of injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions] $s_A:A\to I_A^\bullet$, $s_B:B\to I_B^\bullet$, $s_C:C\to I_C^\bullet$ with $I_A^q=I_B^q=I_C^q=0$ for $q<0$ (so $0\to X\xrightarrow{s_X}I_X^0\to I_X^1\to\cdots$ is exact for $X=A,B,C$) and morphisms of complexes $\alpha:I_A^\bullet\to I_B^\bullet$, $\beta:I_B^\bullet\to I_C^\bullet$ with $\alpha^0s_A=s_Bf$, $\beta^0s_B=s_Cg$ and $0\to I_A^n\xrightarrow{\alpha^n}I_B^n\xrightarrow{\beta^n}I_C^n\to0$ short exact for every $n\ge0$. Let $S':0\to A'\xrightarrow{f'}B'\xrightarrow{g'}C'\to0$ be a second short exact sequence, $(a,b,c)$ a morphism from $S$ to $S'$ (morphisms $a:A\to A'$, $b:B\to B'$, $c:C\to C'$ with $bf=f'a$, $cg=g'b$), $(s_A,s_B,s_C,\alpha,\beta)$ a horseshoe resolution of $S$ and $(s'_{A'},s'_{B'},s'_{C'},\alpha',\beta')$ a horseshoe resolution of $S'$, with complexes $I_{A'}'^\bullet,I_{B'}'^\bullet,I_{C'}'^\bullet$. Let $\varphi_A:I_A^\bullet\to I_{A'}'^\bullet$ and $\varphi_C:I_C^\bullet\to I_{C'}'^\bullet$ be any morphisms of complexes with $\varphi_A^0s_A=s'_{A'}a$ and $\varphi_C^0s_C=s'_{C'}c$ (such morphisms exist by [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists]). Then there is a morphism of complexes $\varphi_B:I_B^\bullet\to I_{B'}'^\bullet$ with $\varphi_B^0s_B=s'_{B'}b$, $\varphi_B\circ\alpha=\alpha'\circ\varphi_A$ and $\beta'\circ\varphi_B=\varphi_C\circ\beta$; that is, $(\varphi_A,\varphi_B,\varphi_C)$ is a morphism of short exact sequences of complexes lifting $(a,b,c)$.

source.place: No Stacks statement. Classical: Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, proof of Theorem 2.4.6 (naturality of the connecting maps; dual of the horseshoe Lemma 2.2.8), not in literature/ (WANTED). Stacks ingredients for a proof: homology.tex Lemma Tag 0136 (lemma-characterize-injectives: a short exact sequence starting with an injective splits), derived.tex Lemma Tag 013R (lemma-acyclic-is-zero: a morphism from an acyclic complex to a bounded below complex of injectives is homotopic to zero), derived.tex Lemma Tag 013P (lemma-morphisms-lift, for the existence of phi_A, phi_C). Route found by the worker of lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor (checked by hand, signs included): choose degreewise splittings r, sigma of the rows of the first horseshoe and r', sigma' of the second (0136); chi := alpha' phi_A r + sigma' phi_C beta satisfies chi alpha = alpha' phi_A and beta' chi = phi_C beta; D := d chi - chi d satisfies D alpha = 0 and beta' D = 0, so D^n = alpha' E^n beta for unique E^n: I_C^n -> I'_A^{n+1}, and chi^0 s_B - s'_B b = alpha' e g for a unique e: C -> I'_A^0; then dE + Ed = 0 and E^0 s_C = d e, so u^{-1} = e, u^n = (-1)^n E^n is a morphism from the acyclic augmented complex C -> I_C^0 -> I_C^1 -> ... (C in degree -1) to the complex of injectives with m-th term I'_A^{m+1}; by 013R it is null-homotopic by h^m (h^{-1} = 0); with k^n = (-1)^n h^n one has E^n = d k^n - k^{n+1} d and e = k^0 s_C, and phi_B := chi - alpha' k beta works.

proof.text: **Step 1 (splittings and the preliminary middle map).** Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ses-injective-kernel-splits] degreewise to the two horseshoe rows. Choose $r^n:I_B^n\to I_A^n$, $\sigma^n:I_C^n\to I_B^n$ and $r'^n:I_{B'}'^n\to I_{A'}'^n$, $\sigma'^n:I_{C'}'^n\to I_{B'}'^n$ with $r\alpha=1$, $\beta\sigma=1$, $\alpha r+\sigma\beta=1$ and the analogous primed identities. Set $\chi^n=\alpha'^n\varphi_A^n r^n+\sigma'^n\varphi_C^n\beta^n$. Then $\chi\alpha=\alpha'\varphi_A$ and $\beta'\chi=\varphi_C\beta$, because $\beta'\alpha'=0$, $\beta'\sigma'=1$, $r\alpha=1$, and $\beta\alpha=0$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0136, implication (1) => (3), used for the degreewise splittings in the horseshoe argument

proof.text: **Step 2 (defects factor through the outer terms).** Put $D^n=d_{I_{B'}'}^n\chi^n-\chi^{n+1}d_{I_B}^n$. Since $\chi\alpha=\alpha'\varphi_A$ and $\beta'\chi=\varphi_C\beta$ are morphisms of complexes, $D\alpha=0$ and $\beta'D=0$. Exactness of each primed and unprimed row therefore gives unique maps $E^n:I_C^n\to I_{A'}'^{n+1}$ with $D^n=\alpha'^{n+1}E^n\beta^n$. The identity $d'D-Dd=0$ implies $d'E+Ed=0$ after cancelling the monomorphism $\alpha'$ and epimorphism $\beta$. At degree zero, $w=\chi^0s_B-s'_{B'}b$ vanishes after precomposition with $f$, while $\beta'^0w=0$; hence exactness of $S$ and $S'$ gives a unique $e:C\to I_{A'}'^0$ with $w=\alpha'^0eg$. Comparing $D^0s_B$ in the two factorizations gives $E^0s_C=d_{I_{A'}'}^0e$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 013T, proof of the horseshoe construction; the factorization identities are the standard diagram chase underlying Weibel Theorem 2.4.6

proof.text: **Step 3 (remove the defect by a homotopy).** Adjoin $C$ in degree $-1$ to $I_C^\bullet$ using $s_C:C\to I_C^0$; this augmented complex is acyclic by the resolution hypothesis. Regard $e$ and the signed maps $u^{-1}=e$, $u^n=(-1)^nE^n$ as a morphism from that augmented complex to the shifted complex with terms $I_{A'}'^{m+1}$. The relation $E^0s_C=d'e$ and $d'E+Ed=0$ are exactly the chain-map identities. By [lem-weil-pbc-acyclic-map-to-injective-nullhomotopy], this map is null-homotopic. Writing the resulting homotopy with $h^{-1}=0$ and putting $k^n=(-1)^nh^n$ gives $e=k^0s_C$ and $E^n=d'k^n-k^{n+1}d$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 013R (lemma-acyclic-is-zero), applied to the augmented resolution of C and the shifted bounded-below injective complex

proof.text: **Step 4 (the corrected middle lift).** Define $\varphi_B^n=\chi^n-\alpha'^n k^n\beta^n$. Its differential defect is $D-\alpha'(d'k-kd)\beta=0$, so it is a morphism of complexes. Because $\beta'\alpha'=0$ and $\beta\alpha=0$, it satisfies $\beta'\varphi_B=\varphi_C\beta$ and $\varphi_B\alpha=\alpha'\varphi_A$. Finally, $\varphi_B^0s_B-s'_{B'}b=\alpha'^0(e-k^0s_C)g=0$. Thus $(\varphi_A,\varphi_B,\varphi_C)$ is the required morphism of short exact sequences lifting $(a,b,c)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 013T and the naturality calculation in Weibel Theorem 2.4.6

split_report.summary: Split the imported horseshoe naturality statement into four steps. Degreewise injective splittings give a preliminary middle map; an explicit defect factorization through the outer terms produces a chain map from the augmented C-resolution to a shifted primed A-resolution; the bounded-below injective null-homotopy leaf removes that defect; and the corrected middle map is checked to commute with both rows and augmentations. Added the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-acyclic-map-to-injective-nullhomotopy for Stacks Tag 013R.
